name: Labour movement
title: The story of the labour movement

text: More than 200 years ago in Britain, great numbers of people went to work in cotton mills and coal mines.
Men, women and children worked twelve hours a day or more, with no help if they were hurt or ill.
src: From about 1800 to the present / Arose in Britain with the Industrial Revolution / Cotton mills, ironworks and coal mines gathered great numbers of wage-earners in towns such as Manchester and Glasgow
where men, women and children worked days of twelve hours or more under factory discipline, with no protection against injury, sickness or unemployment

text: Workers joined together in trade unions to ask for better pay, shorter hours and safer work.
At first unions were outlawed, and six farm workers were sent to Australia as punishment for swearing a union oath.
src: factory hands, miners and craftsmen combined in trade unions to bargain over wages, hours and conditions
Outlawed or harassed in its early decades / Six farm labourers from Tolpuddle in Dorset are sentenced to transportation for swearing a union oath / sentenced in 1834 to transportation to Australia

text: The Chartists gathered millions of names on petitions asking for working men to get the vote.
Parliament said no each time, but in the end Britain gave the vote to all men.
src: The Chartists presented three great petitions to Parliament, in 1839, 1842 and 1848, the second with over three million signatures / the vote for working men, the leading demand of the People’s Charter
all were rejected / votes for all men in 1918

text: Keir Hardie, a Scottish miner, became one of the first labour members of Parliament and helped found the Labour Party.
Around the world, workers marched on May Day, 1 May, for an eight-hour working day.
src: Keir Hardie, a Scottish miner who in 1892 became one of the first independent labour members of the British Parliament and helped found the Labour Party
called for demonstrations for the eight-hour day on 1 May 1890 / May Day became the workers’ day across the world

text: In Poland, a union called Solidarity stood up to communist rule.
Since then, fewer people have joined unions in many countries, as mines and factories closed.
src: in 1980 Poland’s Solidarity union challenged communist rule
From the 1980s union membership fell in most industrial countries as coal, steel and manufacturing declined

text: Today the weekend, paid holidays, sick pay and pensions all began as demands of the labour movement.
Many countries keep 1 May as a public holiday.
src: Much of what wage-earners in industrial countries take for granted was first a demand of the labour movement: the eight-hour day and the weekend, paid holidays, factory inspection, sick pay, pensions
1 May is a public holiday in many countries
